metadata.title: A stream of hypervelocity stars from the Galactic Center

evidence.quote: We use S5-HVS1 to anchor our prediction.

Hills (1988) proposed that tidal disruptions of binary stars in the Galactic Center could produce hypervelocity
stars–stars that are fast enough to escape the Galactic potential. In fact, Koposov et al. (2020) recently discovered S5-
HVS1–a 1700 km\mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }hypervelocity star.
In this paper we predict S5-HVS1 is part of a larger stream

notes: S5-HVS1: classified as follow_up because the paper credits Koposov et al. (2020) with discovering it as a 1700 km s−1 hypervelocity star while using it to anchor the GCC-stream prediction (T:p1-b10, T:p2-b3). The supplied paper gives no Gaia or other catalog identifier for it. The S-stars and simulated stream members are not individually identified Galactic-unbound stars.

S5-HVS1: The paper's target S5-HVS1 is used only as an anchor for the mock GCC stream. The only numeric quantity reported for the star itself is its ~1700 km/s velocity (from Koposov et al. 2020), described as a hypervelocity star ejected from the Galactic Center; the paper does not explicitly state whether this is a heliocentric or Galactic-rest-frame speed, nor does it report a radial velocity, distance, parallax, proper motions, or coordinates in numeric form. Figure 3 shows S5-HVS1 as a red square in an Aitoff projection but gives no numerical position, so no position values are extracted.
